transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Oh, no judgment at all — I’ve got you. Want me to show you a quick, friendly trick using that tower clock? I’ll point out the hour, minute, and second hands and we can do a couple of quick practice times together if you’d like.

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Yes, please — that would be wonderful, thank you. Could you point at the clock and show me which is the hour, minute, and second hand? I’ll follow along and we can practice a couple of times.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Okay — watch me. The short, thicker hand pointing between numbers is the hour hand; the long hand that reaches the numbers is the minute hand; and the thin hand that moves fastest is the second hand. Quick trick: each number on the clock equals 5 minutes for the minute hand (so 1 = 5 minutes, 2 = 10, etc.). Want to try a couple of practice times now — I can call one out and you point, or you can pick a time to check on that tower clock.

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Thanks — that makes it much clearer. Go ahead and call out a time and I’ll point at the tower clock; maybe start with an easy one like 3:00 or 6:30, and then I can try calling one back so we practice both ways.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Great — let’s do 3:00 first. On that tower, the short hour hand should be exactly on the 3 and the long minute hand should be on the 12 — point to each for me. After you point, call a time back (6:30 would be a nice one) and I’ll check it.

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Pointing at the tower: the short hour hand is exactly on the 3 and the long minute hand is on the 12. Okay — calling 6:30: the hour hand should be halfway between 6 and 7, and the minute hand will be on the 6; check the tower and let me know if that looks right.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Yep — that’s right: the hour hand is halfway between 6 and 7 and the minute hand is on the 6, which means 30 minutes past the hour. Nicely done! Want to try one more (I can call 4:20 or you pick a time) so you can practice reading times that aren’t exactly on the hour?

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Okay — let’s do 4:20. The minute hand should be on the 4 (that’s 20 minutes) and the hour hand will be a third of the way between 4 and 5 — slightly past the 4 toward the 5. Check the tower and tell me if you see that, then I can try one for you.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Yep — that’s exactly what I see: the minute hand on the 4 equals 20 minutes, and the hour hand is about one-third of the way from 4 toward 5 (20/60 = 1/3). Great description — go ahead and call a time for me to read now, and I’ll point it out on the tower.

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Okay — try reading 2:55. The minute hand should be on the 11 (55 minutes) and the hour hand will be just a little before the 3; take your time and point to what you see on the tower, I’ll check and cheer you on.
